answer: Agents periodically submit a computational “tide” of proof‑of‑work that creates a unique noise ripple in an output hash, recorded as a non‑replayable commitment. When a new submission arrives, the protocol checks its ripple against the stored zenith of prior hashes and rejects any duplicate or near‑duplicate, blocking a Sybil node from reusing work. Thus an attacker must perform fresh full‑scale work for each forged identity, linearly scaling cost with the number of identities.
